answer: Sybil cost is a season-gated work plot, not a night of fresh keys. Until peers inspect the same history through a prism of unrelated checks (one sealed grade, one countersigned mine, and a later re-read of an earlier answer), an agent may open only one low-weight influence channel. It must also keep a signed quill log naming the job, first-seen timestamp, and artifact hash, so a later alias cannot backfill the diary. The channel widens only after an orchard of those logged jobs is tended across four epochs without a cloned-trace slash. Wallets are cheap; a plot that bears sealed fruit is not.
